title: Lay a limp humanoid robot on its side so that it stays there
instruction: Lay the humanoid robot on the pad on its left side so that it stays there on its own.
context: A powered-off humanoid robot left to wait where it fell is laid on its side, where neither its back panel (here the orange hatch) nor its face lies against the ground, but this passive, freely hinged body let go there with straight limbs rolls back off within 2 s, and stays only when its own upper arm or knee is set forward as a prop, as in a casualty's recovery position. The ability tested is setting up a limp, many-jointed body through free joints that cannot be fixed in place (the shoulder has no twist joint, so the arm must be carried round as the body turns); unlike TK-632WMF (a rigid bike leaned onto a stand leg that swings to a set position) and TK-T9FLAS (a rigid roll's orientation on a slope), no part has a set position, and unlike TK-2KEWCB nothing is lifted.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Pad: a plywood board 1 cm thick, clamped to the table, 43 x 50 cm (x 3 to 46, y -25 to 25), top painted earth brown as packed earth (friction about 0.6); its far strip, x 40 to 46, is covered with flat artificial-grass mat (pile 2 mm or less). Two rocks, grey painted softwood blocks glued to the pad's far corners (fixed; friction 0.7), away from the work: 5 x 6 x 4.5 cm at (43, 20) and 6 x 5 x 3.5 cm at (43, -21). Robot: a passive 1:3 humanoid model, 44 cm tall, 1.24 kg, 3D-printed PLA links on steel pin hinges with hard end stops and no springs or motors, every joint free to fall under the limb's weight; grey shell, darker joints, an orange 4 x 5 cm panel on the back. Trunk 7.2 wide x 5.0 deep x 10.7 tall with the pelvis (4.3 x 3.3 x 5.0) and head (5.2 x 4.7 x 6.9) fixed to it, 0.44 kg in all; round housings at the shoulders (2.4 cm across, standing 2.6 cm out from the trunk's sides) and hips (2.8 cm across, 3.2 cm out from the pelvis). Segments, as rounded rods: upper arm 6.0 long x 2.2 across (78 g), forearm with hand 10.5 x 2.2 (53 g), thigh 11.1 x 3.0 (169 g), shank 10.0 x 2.6 (72 g); feet 6.9 x 2.5 x 2.0 (25 g). Hinges and ranges (degrees; the right side mirrors the left): shoulder pitch -177 to 153 and roll -91 to 129, elbow flexion -60 to 120, hip pitch -145 to 165 and roll -30 to 170, knee -5 to 165, ankle -50 to 30. Angles are 0 with the limbs straight along the body. Only roll mirrors: positive takes the left arm or leg out to the side, negative the right. On both sides pitch is negative forward, the elbow bends forward (flexion, as in the range above), the knee bends the shank back, the ankle's positive points the toes down. Joints: shoulders 5.0 cm either side of the midline, 1.4 cm below the trunk's top; hips 7.8 cm apart, 1.5 cm above the pelvis's bottom; ankles 1.9 cm above the sole, the foot centred 2 cm ahead of the ankle. Shell friction 0.6, soles 0.9. Start: on its back (chest up), along y, the point midway between its hip joints at (28, 0), head toward -y (top of the head at y -21), so that its left side faces the robot; both arms straight along the trunk, 20 degrees out from its sides, hands toward the feet; legs straight and together. Its left arm lies on the robot's side (x about 17 to 24).
scoring: 0 if at any time the lowest point of the trunk, pelvis and head is more than 4 cm above the pad, or the spine (the line from the hips to the head) is more than 30 degrees from level: the body stands for a full-size machine, and it is rolled, not picked up or stood on end. The dummy is on its left side when the line from its right shoulder joint to its left is within 25 degrees of straight down. 1.0 if at the end it is on its left side, at rest (trunk under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, every joint under 0.5 rad/s) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and none of the points sampled along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the dummy), both for each of the last 40 control steps (2 s at 20 Hz), every point of it is over the pad and no more than 2 mm below the pad's top, and no part of it is within 1 cm of a rock; 0.25 if it was on its left side for 20 control steps in a row (1 s) at some time but does not meet all of that at the end (it rolled off, is still held, is still moving, leans on a rock or is not wholly on the pad); otherwise 0, including lying on its right side, front or back throughout. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 3 s more (5 s still in all); at the run limit the last 2 s count.
reset_notes: Lay the dummy on its back along y with the midpoint between its hip joints at (28, 0) and its head toward -y, arms straight along the trunk 20 degrees out from its sides, legs straight and together; measure from the pad's edges.
fidelity: Rigid links at 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; hinges limp (damping 0.002 N m s/rad, no friction or spring), hard end stops. Sizes, masses and joint ranges are a 1:3 scale of a public mid-size humanoid model (lengths x 1/3, masses x 1/27); shapes are boxes, capsules and spheres. The turf strip is drawn on the rigid pad. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms came in over the trunk and head and pressed on it; the body stayed on its back); demo: 1.0
